subject: LTFR
title: Intermediate French I
description: First course in a three-quarter sequence designed to prepare students for upper-division French courses. The course is taught entirely in French and emphasizes the development of reading ability, listening comprehension, and conversational and writing skills. Basic techniques of literary analysis.
prerequisites_text: LIFR 1C/CX or its equivalent, score of 3 on French language AP exam or consent of instructor.

subject: LTFR
title: Intermediate French II
description: Second course in a three-quarter sequence designed to prepare students for upper-division French courses. The course is taught entirely in French and emphasizes the development of reading ability, listening comprehension, and conversational and writing skills. Basic techniques of literary analysis.
prerequisites_text: LTFR 2A or its equivalent, score of 4 on French language or score of 3 on French literature AP exams or consent of instructor.

subject: LTFR
title: Intermediate French III: Composition and Cultural Contexts
description: Designed to improve writing and conversational skills. Develop written expression in terms of organization or ideas, structure, vocabulary. Grammar review. Discussions of contemporary novel and film.
prerequisites_text: LTFR 2B or its equivalent, score of 5 on French language or score of 4 on French literature AP exams or consent of instructor.

subject: LTFR
title: Advanced French Reading and Writing
description: This course will help students transition from lower-division French language courses to upper-division literature courses through close work with original texts to develop comprehension, writing, and analytical skills. May be taken for credit up to three times.

subject: LTFR
title: Themes in Intellectual and Literary History
description: Course in a two-quarter sequence designed as an introduction to French literature and literary history. Each quarter will center on a specific theme or problem. It is recommended that majors whose primary literature is French take this sequence as early as possible. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Themes in Intellectual and Literary History
description: Course in a two-quarter sequence designed as an introduction to French literature and literary history. Each quarter will center on a specific theme or problem. It is recommended that majors whose primary literature is French take this sequence as early as possible. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: The Middle Ages and the Renaissance
description: Major literary works of the Middle Ages and Renaissance as seen against the historical and intellectual background of the period. Medieval texts in modern French translation. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Seventeenth-Century French Literature
description: This course will cover major literary works and problems of seventeenth-century French literature. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Eighteenth-Century French Literature
description: Major literary works and problems of the eighteenth century. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Nineteenth-Century French Literature
description: Major literary works of the nineteenth century. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Twentieth-Century French Literature
description: Major literary works and problems of the twentieth century. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Literatures in French
description: Examines one or more periods, themes, authors, and approaches in French literature. Topics will vary with instructor. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Literary Genres in French
description: An examination of one or more major or minor genres of French literature: for example, drama, novel, poetry, satire, prose poem, essay. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Major Authors in French
description: A study in depth of the works of a major French writer. Recommended for students whose primary literature is French. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Topics in Modern French Culture
description: A course on changing topics such as France during the 1960s, contemporary social and cultural structures (the school system, economy, political parties), myths of America in France, etc. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

subject: LTFR
title: Directed Group Study
description: Research seminars and research, under the direction of a member of the staff. May be taken for credit up to nine times. (P/NP grades only.)

subject: LTFR
title: Special Studies
description: Tutorial; individual guided reading in areas of French literature not normally covered in courses. May be taken for credit up to four times. (P/NP grades only.)

subject: LTFR
title: Directed Studies: Reading Course
description: This course may be designed according to an individual student’s needs when seminar offerings do not cover subjects, genres, or authors of interest. No paper required. The 297 courses do not count toward the seminar requirement. Repeatable for credit.

subject: LTFR
title: Special Projects: Writing Course
description: Similar to a 297, but a paper is required. Papers are usually on subjects not covered by seminar offerings. Up to two 298s may be applied toward the twelve-seminar requirement of the doctoral program. Repeatable for credit.

subject: LTFR
title: Dissertation
description: Research for the dissertation. Offered for repeated registration. Open only to PhD students who have advanced to candidacy.
